page: Microsoft Azure D128ps_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpsv7 family, managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 128 dedicated virtual processor cores built on 64-bit ARM architecture paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server contains no integrated graphical processing units.

The hardware configuration does not feature bundled local storage. Operating system installations and transactional data rely entirely on remote storage services, with explicit support for Azure Premium Storage. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided, requiring standard virtual network infrastructure for outbound and inbound connectivity. Workloads deployed to this instance must be compatible with the arm64 instruction set.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution across 128 dedicated cores, the instance provides high compute density on ARM hardware. ARM architecture provides favorable operational efficiency and resource density for parallel tasks compared to x86 alternatives. Common workload targets include multi-threaded web services, containerized application clusters, continuous integration build pipelines, and distributed data processing frameworks built for ARM.
description: Microsoft Azure D128ps_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine from the Dpsv7 family running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by 64-bit ARM architecture, it features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, requiring remote Azure Premium Storage disks for data and operating system volumes, and it includes no integrated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The ARM core design offers efficient resource density for multi-threaded and distributed enterprise environments. Given its high core count and uniform memory distribution, D128ps_v7 fits horizontally scaled web application tiers, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration build servers, and distributed data processing tasks compiled for 64-bit ARM runtime environments.
